correctness.rationale: The conditional count at recognized size ℓ is binom(n−ℓ,k−ℓ)D_(n−k)/(n−ℓ)! = c_(n,k)(k)_(fall ℓ), vanishing when ℓ>k. Thus exactly k=n−1 must be excluded among the interior rows. The Pascal kernel is totally nonnegative and the odds-power kernel has strictly positive increasing-exponent ordered minors for strictly increasing positive odds. In Cauchy–Binet, intermediate columns 0,…,r−1 in the falling-factorial kernel give the ordinary Vandermonde in k, since the column polynomials are monic of degrees 0,…,r−1. That term is strictly positive and all terms are nonnegative. For curvature, reversing the standard Laguerre coefficient sum at degree k and parameter n−k gives the stated odds polynomial with constant term one. Orthogonality on (0,∞) gives k simple positive zeros, hence the stated positive linear factors in θ. Their second log derivatives give the identity; the (1−θ)^(n−k) term is strictly concave if k<n, and otherwise at least one of n≥2 distinct roots is not 1. The exponent also gives score −∞ at θ→1 when a count is <n; at 0 the score is n times the sum of (k−1). All-n data give a strictly increasing likelihood by coupling the binomial recognized size. These checks support the boundary/maximizer claims in RESULT.md lines 33–75. Independent exact subset/permutation enumeration at n=3 gave p_0=(1−θ)^3/3, p_1=1/2−3θ²/2+θ³ and p_3=1/6+θ+θ²/2−2θ³/3. They sum to 1; all ordered minors on the three-parameter grid (1/4,1/2,3/4) were positive, with determinant 11/1024, and the log-curvatures at 1/2 were (−12,−9,−984/289). Inspected verify.py without executing it. The n=3 calculation and supplied finite checks are not all-size proofs.

evidence: The classical basic composition formula gives ordered minors of a product kernel as sums/integrals of products of ordered minors. Galvin–Pacurar identifies the Pascal matrix as totally nonnegative. The odds-power factor is the standard strictly totally positive exponential kernel e^(ℓ log t), scaled by positive factors.
DLMF gives the generalized Laguerre coefficient identity, positive weight x^α e^(−x) on the positive axis and the simple orthogonality-interval zeros theorem, with α=n−k≥0 here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strict×strict clause of the composition theorem should not be applied to a triangular Pascal kernel. Instead the exact formula (5.14) gives strictness for any finite totally nonnegative first factor of full row rank and any strictly totally positive second kernel: every selected row subset has a positive maximal minor and every corresponding second minor is positive. The retained Pascal rows are linearly independent rows of an invertible triangular matrix, and the factorial/binomial and probability prefactors are positive. This supplies all orders, not only order two. The known root theorem likewise applies to all retained counts.

evidence: O'Neill's recognized count is binomial with parameter θ and his conditional completion is the classical fixed-point law on the remaining n−ℓ positions. It is the same total K, not the recognized count. The conditional coefficient rearranges to c_(n,k) ℓ! binom(k,ℓ).

After row scaling and changing θ to positive odds t, the polynomial coefficients are binom(n,ℓ)binom(k,ℓ)ℓ!, counting ℓ-edge matchings of K_(n,k), equivalently nonattacking rooks on the n×k board. Equation (18.5.12) is the exact reversed-Laguerre coefficient formula for this polynomial.
